source_text.body:
Build a Next.js directory app in one shot
Poster had Manus build a Next.js directory app and then QA and fix bugs; the result was structurally promising but needed human correction.
Done with
MA
Manus
What they did
The poster gave Manus a detailed prompt to build a simple Next.js and Tailwind directory app with milestones, seed script, search, admin dashboard, and Docker. Manus planned the work, checked in at each milestone, and finished in about 40 minutes with quick human replies, but when asked to start the dev server and then run its own QA and bug-fixing pass, it still could not get the app running.
How it went
The structure looked promising, but the delivered app had simple React runtime errors, incomplete UI, and functionality the poster judged only okay-ish. They spent 1,643 credits total, about $16.43, and ended up relying on GPT-4o to spot at least one obvious issue.
Worth knowing
The main catch was cost versus reliability: the initial build, bug-fix pass, and project archive together used 1,643 credits even though the app never reached a working state.
Try it yourself
with
Manus
Copy prompt
Build a Next.js directory app for [topic, e.g. local coffee shops] with listings, search, category filters, and a detail page for each entry, seeded with [number] sample entries. When it's built, test it yourself, fix any bugs you find, and give me a list of what you tested and any known issues remaining. Done when the app runs and the main flows work. Ask me before connecting any paid services or deploying it.
Original source: https://www.reddit.com/r/ManusOfficial/comments/1k6oe1r/my_experience_using_manus_to_build_a_nextjs
